source_groups.label: Time-to-equatorial-degree table, exact 15-degree-per-hour linear relation
claims: table_heading
Table converting Hours and Minutes of time into Degrees and Minutes of the Aequator
The new natality introduction begins with a tabular conversion of clock time into equatorial angular displacement.
Numerical/astronomical conversion, not event prediction.
table_rule
one Hour fifteen degrees
One hour of time corresponds to fifteen degrees of the equator.
360 degrees divided by 24 hours.
table_rule
24 Hours 360 degrees
The twenty-four-hour row corresponds to a complete 360-degree rotation.
Full-turn modulo 360 applies in subsequent computation.
table_rule
one minute time fifteen minutes equator
One minute of clock time corresponds to fifteen arcminutes of equatorial angle.
0.25 angular degrees per minute of time.
table_rule
four minutes time one degree
Four minutes of civil time correspond to one angular degree.
Reciprocal form used later as minutes divided by four.
table_image_preservation
columns hour degree minute time minute angle
The printed reference has separate hour-to-degree and minute-to-degree columns with row values.
Complete table numerals require independent transcription; only structure and load-bearing examples checked.
table_example
60 minutes time fifteen degrees
Sixty time minutes correspond to fifteen degrees.
Source last minute row is visibly printed as sixty to fifteen degrees.

Historical house-construction algorithm.
method

Numerical rule repeated from printed table.
method

Scale factor, not new independent observation.
method

method

source_groups.label: MC to ascendant +90° printed discrepancy crossing source pages
claims: method
add ninety degrees to Mid-heaven RA
Lilly instructs adding 90° to right ascension of the tenth-house cusp before Ascendant lookup.
This is the formal step of his Regiomontanus house-construction procedure.
original_numeric_claim
142.20 plus 90 printed 230.20
The first-edition print appears to claim adding 90° to 142°20′ produces 230°20′.
Numerically false: 142°20′ + 90° = 232°20′, a two-degree discrepancy. Do not silently repair either printed value.
mathematical_check
142.20 and ninety degrees
Independent integer-arcminute arithmetic gives 232°20′.
Contradicts the printed 230°20′, retained as explicit historical numerical error.
method
Table of Oblique ascensions belonging to 53 latitude
He routes the result into the oblique-ascension table corresponding to geographic latitude 53°.
Latitude-specific data rather than universal sign mapping.
source_continuation
degree of the ascendant for that Elevation
The description of using the 53° oblique table to find the Ascendant continues onto PDF525.
One continuous calculation, not separate horoscopes.

method

Interpolation interval and rounding should be verified before encoding a fully reliable calculator.
source_internal_result

Numerical result depends on the internally inconsistent 230°20′ premise.
authorial_scope
more exact nativity than ordinary questions
He distinguishes precise nativity figure computation from less meticulous ordinary horary questions.
A method preference, not empirical evidence natal charts are accurate.
method

Lilly indicates the following four tabular groupings support erecting a figure.
Count refers to groups/types, whereas the full physical source runs over many page faces.
authorial_scope
teach Tyroes
The examples are pedagogical approximations for beginning students.
An introduction rather than a fully worked independent rectification outcome.
